P1.evidence: This call was decided in the first ninety seconds. There was a KL setter suffix on the file but no notes were referenced or read back. The frame ran the usual two of four parts. Before frame agreement could be taken, the prospect seized control and set his own terms: 'if it's like $2,000, I'm good. If it's like eight or nine, I'm out. So we could probably mainstream this a little bit more. You don't have to know all my emotional stuff.' The open question was therefore never asked at all. The rep accepted the new frame without contest and never attempted to re-establish the process, which is the root cause of every subsequent phase failing.

P2.evidence: Almost no baseline was taken. Age was volunteered ('I'm 50'), height and weight were never asked. Occupation was volunteered in the opening ultimatum and never explored as a work-pattern question. General health conditions were never asked. The one genuine question was on injuries - 'As far as your injuries, what type of injuries are you maybe rehabbing from?' - which produced a car accident, herniations at L5-S1 and L4-L5, and a microdiscectomy, and it was not followed up on duration, current restriction, or whether loaded ballistic work is appropriate. Training frequency was never established at all: on a 24-minute call with a self-taught kettlebell trainee, nobody asked how many days a week he trains. Diet was never asked despite the prospect raising body fat twice and volunteering that nutrition is his gap. Sleep and energy were never touched.

P3.evidence: One good question - 'when you say that you're trying to work on your aesthetics, is that, what does that look like?' - produced upper body, thighs and body fat. Nothing else in the phase ran. The prospect volunteered the entire deep layer unprompted and it was left where it landed: 'I'm 50, and I want to continue doing all this stuff for the next 20, 30 years. I don't want to have to give up anything else because I'm too old and broken.' That is a longevity and identity answer handed over free, and the rep replied 'Yeah, 100%' and asked about injuries. The single largest omission on the call comes later, when he volunteered a five-year-old son and eight-year-old daughter copying his kettlebell workouts and said he wants to teach them 'so they don't mess up their freaking back'. The rep said 'Yeah, 100%' and moved to the accountability pitch. Who else this impacts, and the drive through to kids and legacy, were sitting in the transcript and were not picked up.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase on the call. Past attempts were asked properly - 'have you specifically reached out to anyone for education around the kettlebells' - producing the Ben Patrick knees-over-toes programme with video form analysis, and the follow-up 'did that help when they were analyzing your videos and sending back to you? Like did you get value out of that?' produced the single most important sentence in the transcript: 'it was a delayed response because I had to go through the trouble of filming it, and then I'd send it, and then I had to wait for them, and for the work, I'm not sure the juice was worth the squeeze.' The prospect had already tried and rejected the exact delivery mechanism the programme uses. The rep asked the right question, got a decisive answer, and then pitched asynchronous video form review anyway. The root cause was never named and no structural gap was surfaced.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form - the fifth consecutive sales call in this batch with the entire 20-point Consequence Frame absent, and the one where the raw material was richest. A car accident, two herniations, a spinal surgery paid $11,000 out of pocket, flare-ups on every hard training block, a stated fear of being 'too old and broken', and two young children learning movement by watching him. A two-year question here writes itself and not one of the four checks was attempted.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The rep went from the three-phase presentation directly to 'really the only thing left to discuss is like next steps, investment, all that.' No belief question, no all-in question, and no verbal yes was taken before the price was spoken. When the prospect had earlier said 'None. I don't have any questions', that was treated as agreement rather than tested.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and failed. No payment was collected, no link was sent, and no follow-up was scheduled. The onboarding steps were described in advance as what would happen - 'as soon as we figure out the investment, we get you access to everything right away... He'll send you a little questionnaire' - but were never reached.

objection_plays.detail: A money-shaped trigger that was not a money objection, and the rep diagnosed it wrong. He ran one move - the offer to break the payment up, 'Even if we split it up for you' - and was immediately corrected: 'Oh, it's not that. I can afford it. But just because I can afford it doesn't mean I should.' None of the rest ran: no isolate, no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no financial picture questions, and no permission-to-talk-openly question. The correct read was available from the opening ninety seconds, where the prospect framed his ceiling in value terms and disclosed he sells $10,000 packages himself. Once affordability was ruled out the rep had nothing left, because the play he was running had already been disproved.

The prospect used the word himself, twice: 'My fear, my fear is that I would get in this program and I would be like, this isn't any different than me watching some of these videos.' The rep opened by conceding it - 'I guess you don't really know until you're in it' - which is the opposite of the scripted position, and then differentiated on feedback. None of the actual moves ran: no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure-versus-pain question, no bridge or plane frame, no burned-before frame. Most notably 'how will you know if you never actually try' was the precise answer to the objection as stated and the rep said the inverse of it. No risk reversal, guarantee or trial was offered to a prospect whose entire block was uncertainty of outcome.
No think-about-it deferral. The prospect gave a clean decision on the call rather than asking for time.
No spousal consult, despite his wife training alongside him. The decision was framed entirely as his own.
No timing objection. He was ready to buy something on the call, just not this at this price.

Three unscripted situations, and the first is a new gap worth adding to the known list. (1) A prospect who cancels discovery and pre-anchors price in the opening ninety seconds - 'we could probably mainstream this a little bit more. You don't have to know all my emotional stuff' - delivered by someone who sells high ticket himself and recognises the process being run on him. There is no scripted way to reclaim the frame, and the rep simply complied. (2) A cheaper alternative that genuinely worked: eighteen months of free YouTube kettlebell training that made his spine feel stronger. (3) The delivery mechanism pre-invalidated: he had already used asynchronous video form review on another programme and judged it not worth the effort, so the central differentiator of the pitch was dead on arrival and the script offers nothing else to differentiate with.

notes: The whole call turns on the first ninety seconds, where the prospect set the terms and the rep accepted them. Coach the reclaim: a prospect who says 'you don't have to know all my emotional stuff' can be answered with agreement plus a condition, keeping two or three questions that make a value case possible. Two concrete errors follow from it - pitching asynchronous video review to the one prospect who had explicitly tested and rejected it, and failing to mention the $199 lower tier to a prospect who asked in plain words whether another version existed and said he would pay for the nutrition piece on its own.
